judged_text: The migration interpolates each legacy embeddable_hosts setting line directly into an unescaped SQL string (execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"), so a single quote in any stored host line breaks out of the string literal and executes arbitrary SQL during migration. An operator upgrading a site whose embeddable_hosts value contains a quote character — whether from a past admin entry, a site import, or a restored backup — has attacker-influenced SQL executed with full database privileges at deploy time; even a benign apostrophe aborts the migration and blocks the upgrade for the whole instance.

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb the migration builds raw SQL with string interpolation: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts ... VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. `h` comes from splitting the existing `site_settings` value for `embeddable_hosts` (`val.split("\n")`) and is not escaped/quoted safely. A single quote in `h` would break the SQL string and could lead to unintended SQL execution or at minimum a migration failure, blocking upgrades. This is a verifiable security/correctness defect in the diff.
